mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign parent corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or competent corporate registrar in the foreign shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: 1) Certified notarization by a local public notary; 2) Hague Apostille by the Designated Competent Authority if the home state is a party to the Apostille Convention; OR Consular Legalization at the Consular Section of the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in that home state if the home state is not an Apostille party; 3) Certified Mandarin translation. The Apostille and Consular Legalization routes are parallel and mutually exclusive and are never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Active Status of the foreign parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent government registry in the foreign parent's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: 1) Notarization by a local public notary; 2) Hague Apostille by the home state's Apostille competent authority for Apostille members; OR Consular Legalization by the Chinese Embassy/Consulate for non-members; 3) Certified Chinese translation. Apostille and Consular Legalization are alternating paths; they must not be sequenced together.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution authorizing incorporation of the Chinese WFOE and appointing the legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or corporate secretary of the foreign parent, notarized in the home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: 1) Notarization by a local public notary; 2) Hague Apostille by the home state's competent authority (Apostille Convention states only); OR Consular Legalization at the Chinese Consular post (non-member states); 3) Certified Chinese translation. The two authentication mechanisms are separate and exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum of Association of the foreign parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign companies registry or registered agent in the home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: 1) Certified copy notarized locally; 2) Hague Apostille by the state's designated authority; OR Consular Legalization by the Chinese Embassy/Consulate; 3) Certified Chinese translation of the full instrument. Apostille path is never combined with Consular Legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter issued for the foreign parent's principal banking relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Principal relationship bank of the foreign parent, on official bank letterhead with responsible officer signature
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: 1) Notarization of the bank officer's signature and authority; 2) Hague Apostille by the home state's competent authority if an Apostille member; OR Consular Legalization if a non-member; 3) Certified Chinese translation. Alternative authenticated SWIFT confirmation may supplement, but not replace, the required legalized Bank Reference Letter in this mandatory bundle.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the local incorporation service agent and the first legal representative of the WFOE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign parent company, notarized by a local notary in the parent's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: 1) Notarization of execution; 2) Hague Apostille in Apostille member states; OR Consular Legalization in non-member states; 3) Certified Chinese translation. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must be selected strictly according to the home state's Hague membership status.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before any filing, every shareholder, beneficial owner, director, legal representative, supervisor, senior manager, and authorized signatory must be screened against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT Consolidated List, and Chinese Ministry of Public Security anti-terrorism and tax non-payment lists. Enhanced due diligence is triggered for any PEP, family member, close associate, source of politically exposed wealth, or residency in high-risk jurisdiction. AML/CFT risk score, negative news, watchlist matches, and document verification must be recorded and kept for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Self-Service Declaration System and local Market Regulation Bureau Name Clearance Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Registered enterprise names must be in simplified Chinese characters and must follow the statutory four-tier structure: administrative division + distinctive trade name + industry description + limited company. A WFOE may use a Pinyin or phonetic transliteration of the foreign parent's trade name as the distinctive trade name, but the English-only corporate name is not the registered statutory name. Any English trade name may only be used commercially after the Chinese statutory name has been approved and registered.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant should first obtain the written rejection decision and correct the specific violation by re-declaring a new name on the SAMR portal. If the refusal persists, a written administrative reconsideration application must be filed within 60 days with the market regulation administration at the next higher level, attaching all supporting documents, the foreign investment certificate, and the legal premise for eligibility. Alternatively, the applicant may institute administrative litigation within six months before the competent People's Court in the location of the registry under the Administrative Litigation Law. The name reservation cannot be extended beyond 30 days; a new reservation must be filed after each rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a WFOE engaged in NVOCC/ocean freight forwarding, virtual offices and commercial mailboxes are not permissible as the sole registered office. The NVOCC filing regime and international freight forwarding licensing rules require a fixed, non-mailbox business premise in the registered locality. Local tax authorities reject de-registered virtual addresses for VAT invoice control and may de-rate input VAT. Banks, under PBOC e-KYC guidance, require site inspection, original lease contract, proof of physical office, landlord consent, and utility bills. A serviced office with a dedicated leased suite may be accepted only if the lease term exceeds 12 months and it is not a pure virtual address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: high, approximately 70-80%, that SAMR or municipal tax authority will conduct an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months after VAT invoice issuance, and MOFCOM/local transport authority may inspect NVOCC filings within 6 months. Checklist: display the business license and NVOCC registration at the registered address; maintain original lease contract and rent payment records; keep at least one full-time employee or the legal representative present during business hours; staff the office during business hours; keep books and contracts at the address; install a nameplate matching the registered Chinese name; respond to registry notices within 15 days; preserve utility bills and lease invoices for tax verification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision), Articles 23, 26, 32-38, 46-47, 59-74 and 89-94; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 4, 28, 29 and 31; Regulations on the Registration Administration of Market Entities (2022 Revision), Articles 6-12 and 16-22; Regulations of the People's Republic of China on International Ocean Shipping (2019), Articles 5-7, 25-37.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Market Entity Registration Bureau of the local Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) at the WFOE's registered address; the national SAMR policies are administered through the One-Stop Enterprise Registration portal and the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Market Entity (Company Establishment Registration Application Form) together with the approved Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum registered capital for an ordinary WFOE under the Company Law (2023); the Articles may state any amount, but the shareholder must pay the subscribed capital within five years from establishment. No SAMR escrow or blocked share-capital account is required at incorporation. However, to hold an NVOCC registration, the company must maintain a restricted RMB 800,000 business guarantee or an equivalent MOT-approved bank guarantee with the Ministry of Transport; this is a commercial guarantee, not a corporate paid-in capital escrow.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF CN WFOE LTD. WHEREAS, CN WFOE LTD, the Company, is a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company organized under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China; and WHEREAS, the sole shareholder has appointed the initial directors of the Company in accordance

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA) / China Tax Service electronic portal (Electronic Tax Bureau e-Tax) at etax.chinatax.gov.cn; coordinated with the General Administration of Customs (GACC) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) for export/fx linkage.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the WFOE, after incorporation the Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) issues a business license bearing the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which serves as the legal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) for the entity. Within 30 calendar days from the business license date, the WFOE must complete tax registration on the STA Electronic Tax Bureau using the USCC and AMR record. The STA will activate the entity's period filing calendar, VAT taxpayer profile, invoice quota, e-invoice credentials, export-tax refund/customs status, and non-resident withholding obligations. A foreign non-resident enterprise without a Chinese WFOE or permanent establishment must register for income-tax-withholding purposes with the STA office of the place where the China-source income arises or where the withholding agent is situated; the non-resident is then assigned a separate non-resident Chinese Tax Identification Number after filing the constitutive documents, home-country tax certificate, board resolution, contract with the withholding agent, bank account confirmation, and a description of the China-source activity. This non-resident TIN is used for quarterly/incident withholding declarations and for any self-declared China-source taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the WFOE is mandatorily a Chinese resident enterprise subject to Corporate Income Tax at 25% on its worldwide income; it is not a pass-through vehicle, and no free-zone exemption applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None: PRC law does not provide check-the-box pass-through elections, entity classification elections, or hybrid-mismatch elections for a WFOE limited-liability company. The taxpayer may only select applicable accounting/filing periods, VAT general versus small-scale taxpayer treatment, and APA/treaty tax protections, none of which change entity-level CIT status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the PRC Value-Added Tax Law and the State Taxation Administration implementing rules; export goods and qualifying cross-border services are zero-rated in the VAT ledger.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration where annual taxable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000 (RMB 5,000,000). There is no turnover threshold for normal tax registration: every WFOE must register with the STA within 30 days of issuance of the business license, and must register/self-confirm VAT taxpayer status before issuing VAT invoices or claiming input VAT credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates the Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoice (FDI) regime integrated with the Golden Tax System Phase IV. All VAT invoices must be issued through the STA's official electronic invoice platform or an STA-certified third-party API and must carry a centrally allocated invoice number, a tax-control digital certificate/signature, and an encrypted anti-fraud stamp. Invoice data are transmitted to the STA in real time or on a near-real-time accepted-clearance basis; paper invoices, over-the-counter manual invoices, or unregistered printing devices cannot substantiate input VAT credits or zero-rated export treatment. The tax authority exchanges invoice data with GACC customs declarations and SAFE foreign-exchange receipts for triangulation audits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available (1) for goods physically exported from China and cleared by GACC as exports, and (2) for qualifying cross-border services in the STA catalogue, including international sea carriage and directly ancillary international freight-forwarding/NVOCC services, provided by a VAT general taxpayer to a non-resident enterprise and consumed wholly outside China. For the NVOCC WFOE, the 0% VAT rate is substantiated by showing the recipient of the freight-forwarding service is an overseas shipper/consignee or overseas carrier, the service fee is payable in foreign currency from outside China and is ultimately repatriated, and the movement involves an export customs declaration and an ocean bill of lading from a Chinese port to an overseas port. Domestic pre-carriage, warehousing, customs clearance, and other services inside China remain taxable at the applicable domestic VAT rate unless separately listed in the zero-rated/exempt catalogue.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / Bill of Entry (GACC-approved electronic export customs clearance record) showing HS codes, quantity, FOB value, exporter, and container/trailer identifiers.

Ocean Bill of Lading (B/L) or sea waybill issued by the ocean carrier or NVOCC showing the Chinese origin port, overseas destination port, cargo description, container numbers, and freight payable terms.
Export sales contract and commercial invoice in foreign currency with Incoterms, overseas buyer details, and invoice value traceable to the bank receipt.
Packing list, certificate of origin (if requested), export inspection records, and any export-license/permit document required by Chinese export control rules.

Inward Remittance Certificate / Export Receipts Confirmation issued by a Chinese bank under SAFE rules, or the electronic bank transaction record showing the inbound SWIFT/ACH credit from the overseas customer matching the invoice and customs value.
SAFE trade-in-goods collection and monitoring record evidencing timely repatriation/collection of export proceeds and the matching business transaction number.

NVOCC service agreement, master ocean bill, container-transfer and cargo-tracking evidence, and the foreign-currency settlement voucher proving that the cross-border freight-forwarding fee was received from abroad and consumed outside China.
The VAT electronic export-tax-refund declaration and the STA's returned confirmation file where input VAT refund is claimed for the zero-rated supply.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA, GACC, and SAFE jointly perform export data triangulation: customs declarations, digital VAT invoices, bills of lading, bank foreign-exchange credits, and service contracts are matched automatically. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days, or submission of false B/L/customs/fx evidence, causes the 0% rate to be reversed, input VAT refunds clawed back, and a daily overdue surcharge of 0.05% (or the statutory equivalent) running from the date the refund was paid or the tax should have been paid. Under the PRC Tax Administration Law, fraudulent export-tax-refund filings expose the entity to an administrative penalty of 0.5 to 5 times the fraudulently obtained refund; criminal liability may arise under the Criminal Law for fraudulent export tax refund, including imprisonment and confiscation of assets. The entity is additionally placed on the STA serious-tax-dishonesty joint punishment list, downgraded in customs AEO/credit grading, restricted from export-tax-refund processing, and barred from favorable foreign-exchange management classification until the issue is rectified.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a current-account-convertible but capital-account-administered foreign exchange regime. All cross-border receipts and payments on current account, including freight forwarding service revenues, must be supported by authentic documentation and are generally freely convertible at market rates through authorized banks. Capital account transactions, such as direct investment capital contributions and inbound loans, require prior registration with SAFE and are subject to real-deal verification and payment-through supervision. The RMB is not freely convertible for capital account purposes; thus, a WFOE must open a dedicated Foreign Exchange Capital Account for inbound equity funding and may only settle that capital into RMB with a specific declared payment purpose. Repatriation of profits is lawful after issuance of audited statutory financial statements, full corporate income tax (CIT) settlement, and submission of a board resolution for dividend distribution, but the bank will require a tax certificate showing that all withholding tax obligations are discharged. Current account convertibility also means that an NVOCC receiving USD, EUR, or other currencies from overseas customers can sell those funds to a commercial bank or retain them in a foreign currency current account; however, no automatic convertibility exists for speculative or investment-driven flows. Enterprises must integrate their operations with the full set of SAFE reporting systems and honor transactional documentary rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Mandatory conversion ratio is 0% (abolished by the 2012 SAFE foreign exchange administration reform); enterprises are free to retain export earnings in foreign currency or voluntarily convert to RMB. Statutory repatriation requires that all export proceeds be received into China through a designated bank within the contractual due date, and for goods exports, generally within 90 days from customs export declaration; service-trade proceeds (including NVOCC freight earnings) follow the contract terms and must be remitted within the contract-validity period, normally within one year. The receiving bank conducts a documentary audit via the National Foreign Exchange Verification System (for goods) and the Service Trade Foreign Exchange Information System (for services), and any delayed or abnormal recovery triggers a report to SAFE and may require an extension application.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account (FDI) plus RMB Basic Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Currency Account
Basic Deposit Account (RMB) and Foreign Currency Current Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. Under PBOC/SAFE licensing rules, a fintech electronic money institution (EMI) or digital payment provider may not independently open a settlement account or process cross-border payments for a mainland WFOE unless it has been granted a dedicated cross-border RMB/foreign settlement license. Overseas EMIs (e.g., non-Chinese licensed electronic money issuers) generally do not meet the regulatory definition of a bank in China and are barred from servicing a WFOE's main operational currency flows. A fintech solution may only be used as a front-end interface to a licensed onshore bank or an approved cross-border payment institution (like a licensed third-party payment company with SAFE approval), and even then it cannot replace the mandated bank accounts for capital injection, tax payments, or profit remittance. Therefore, the WFOE should rely exclusively on Tier-1 domestic commercial banks for its primary liquidity rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory legal representative must generally attend an in-branch interview in mainland China when opening the first bank account, presenting the original entry visa/passport and the WFOE's certificate of incorporation. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted for the initial account; however, after the representative completes the in-person interview, the board may appoint a China-based finance manager as an account operator through a notarized and apostilled power of attorney. For foreign legal representatives who are unable to travel, an alternative is to apply with a Chinese notary office for a power of attorney to a local proxy, but the bank will still require at least one video-to-face interview for the statutory director or a senior site visit. Enhanced due diligence for the NVOCC sector will also necessitate a physical visit by a bank compliance officer to the WFOE's registered operation office.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder/beneficial owner is a foreign shell corporation with layered nominee shareholding and opaque trust structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Furnish a full beneficial ownership cascade up to natural persons holding 25% or more; include notarized certificates of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, registers of directors/shareholders for each hop in the chain, final individual passport/citizenship identification, proof of address, and a written source-of-wealth statement evidencing the lawful origin of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based AML signals: freight invoices, bills of lading, and customs declarations do not match in goods description, volume, or value, or the route involves restricted/high-risk corridors (e.g., sanctions hit transshipment points)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a complete transaction file per shipment: commercial contract/booking note, MB/L and HB/L, master vessel IMO number and AIS tracking data, container tracking history from the shipping line, customs export/import matching screenshots, insurance certificate, and a benchmarking of the applied freight rate against the Shanghai Containerized Freight Index (SCFI) or other reputable market indices to substantiate a commercial range.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/PEP screening failure at counterparty or beneficiary level: counterparties, shipping agents, or underlying customers appear on any OFAC/EU/UN/Swiss/SECO sanctions list or are domiciled in an embargoed territory
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a professional compliance certificate from a reputable KYC screening service covering all counterparties, shipping lines, truckers, freight forwarders, and beneficial owners; include a sanctions/embargo radar mapping of all cargo routes; and provide a contractual warranty that no sanctioned cargo will be carried. If any PEP is identified, deliver a comprehensive PEP due diligence file including a justified rationale, transactional profile, and senior management approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dividend/profit repatriation disproportionate to realized revenue and net assets, indicating possible round-tripping or capital flight
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver two years of audited statutory financial statements in Chinese/English, corporate income tax annual settlement filings, VAT filings, the board resolution approving the dividend, and a certified confirmation from the Chinese tax bureau that the WFOE has no outstanding tax liabilities; additionally provide the certificate of the SAFE registration and an explanation of the dividend payout ratio consistent with the WFOE's actual operational profits.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The global parent should remit the equity contribution via SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's designated SAFE-registered Foreign Exchange Capital Account with a stated purpose code for 'FDI paid-in capital' (the bank will map the correct trade code, e.g., 929 or the bank-specific equivalent). The remittance must reference the FDI Foreign Exchange Registration Certificate and the unique SAFE registration number; after credit, the receiving bank issues a capital settlement confirmation and a Chinese CPA performs a capital verification (expert audit) and issues a capital verification report. The capital funds may be converted into RMB for cash operating expenses only after a payment-purpose verification, i.e., the 'payment-through' rule, cannot be used for equity investments or non-commercial real estate purchases, and each RMB conversion must match a specific pending invoice or contract.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement for NVOCC operations (line haul, terminal handling, trucking, pilotage, agency charges, bunkering, insurance) should be routed through SWIFT MT103 for immediate high-value payments, with the bank retained as an instructing customer. Low-value repetitive payments can be batched through domestic ACH and then sent by MT103 to overseas counterparties. For capital-intensive expenditures such as purchase of containers or vessel charter agreements, a commercial letter of credit (L/C) or a documentary collection can be used; the WFOE will submit the transport contract, commercial invoice, tax voucher and SAFE registration for service trade payments (in the relevant Service Trade Foreign Exchange system) before each disbursement. All cross-border payments require the bank to verify the transaction background and cross-border FX purpose code, and the WFOE must keep the complete underlying transport documentation for five years for possible SAFE review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (settlement and sale of forward exchange) onshore for major currencies (USD/CNY, EUR/CNY) with supporting real trade documentation
FX swaps and currency swaps approved by the bank under the interbank FX market, provided the transaction hedge is for a proven current account or capital account exposure
FX options (plain vanilla) for hedging periodic account receivables/payables, not for speculative trading
Offshore NDFs are not permissible onshore for the WFOE; the offshore parent may trade CNH NDFs outside mainland China but cannot book them in the WFOE's accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than June 30 for the preceding calendar year; the filing window opens on January 1 and no extension is available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The enterprise is placed on the abnormal operations list within 10 working days after the deadline; if no correction is made for three consecutive years, it enters the serious illegal and dishonest list with restrictions on the legal representative and responsible managers, and the SAMR may revoke the business license where the company is shown not to have carried on business for an uninterrupted six-month period

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation jointly with the Ministry of Commerce through the consolidated enterprise annual reporting platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than June 30 for the immediately preceding calendar year, filed together with the enterprise annual information report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The market supervision authority orders rectification; failure to rectify triggers an administrative fine of RMB 100,000 to RMB 300,000, or RMB 300,000 to RMB 500,000 for serious circumstances, plus separate fines on the legal representative and responsible persons and potential revocation of the WFOE registration for continued refusal

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Settlement and Final Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration local competent tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than May 31 following the calendar tax year for the enterprise income tax final settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment attracts daily interest of 0.05% of the overdue amount; understatement or non-filing is subject to 50% to 500% administrative penalties, compulsory tax collection from bank deposits and receivables, and, in repeated or fraudulent cases, criminal referral or revocation of the business license

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: NVOCC Annual Operation Report and Deposit Maintenance Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Transport and the local transport authority for the registered address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than March 31 for the prior calendar year; any deposit or operational change must be updated within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain the NVOCC deposit or file the annual operation report results in suspension of the NVOCC record-filing and prohibition on issuing ocean bills of lading; continued non-compliance may lead to cancellation of the record-filing, an administrative fine, and written closure of the freight-forwarding operation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Confirmation and Shareholder Register Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation through the integrated corporate registration and beneficial-owner information portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: In each no-change year, confirm the beneficial-owner schedule with the annual report no later than June 30; any shareholding transfer or change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be filed with SAMR within 30 days after the corporate registration of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-confirmation or knowingly false beneficial-owner filings subject the WFOE to an administrative fine of up to RMB 500,000 with additional responsibility borne by the legal representative, and the SAMR may attach an administrative restrictive mark on the enterprise registration until corrected

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A certified CPA audit of the annual financial statements is compulsory for a PRC WFOE when any of the following criteria is met: total assets at the reporting date reach or exceed RMB 30 million; annual operating revenue for the preceding financial year reaches or exceeds RMB 30 million; average annual headcount for the preceding financial year is 300 or more; the company is placed under abnormal operations or serious dishonest-list enforcement and the SAMR or State Taxation Administration issues a formal audit-demand letter; the company must substantiate the NVOCC deposit guarantee or must provide audited financial statements to the bank, insurance guarantor, foreign shareholder or tax authority for dividend remittance; or the company is engaged in a regulated financial, insurance, securities, fund management or payment activity even without meeting the numeric thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (China GAAP), including the Ministry of Finance implementation notices and measurement requirements; CAS is substantially aligned with IFRS but IFRS as issued by the IASB is not an acceptable primary basis for statutory annual accounts in China.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The WFOE must maintain a beneficial-owner register identifying every natural person who directly or indirectly holds or controls 25% or more of equity or voting rights, or who exercises control through management-appointment arrangements, senior-management power, or contractual agreements. The register and shareholder register are reconciled during the annual secretarial review, and the current beneficial-owner schedule is confirmed through the SAMR annual report no later than June 30. All subsequent share transfers, new-subscriber admissions, equity changes, or control changes are filed with SAMR and the beneficial-owner portal within 30 days after the corporate records are updated, and the statutory books are made available at the registered office for inspection by SAMR, the tax authority, or the courts on demand.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholder and Board Resolutions

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Resident WFOE is generally subject to 25% CIT; a qualified High-and-New-Technology Enterprise may elect a 15% preferential rate; encouraged-region and selected Free-Trade-Zone key-industry WFOEs may access a 15% rate for permitted eligible industries; small-and-micro profit enterprises may enjoy reduced effective rate as low as 5% on qualifying annual taxable income, but such benefit must be substantiated and protected from aggressive transfer pricing adjustments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Main Form A100000) and related supporting schedules, filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax portal in the Electronic Tax Bureau filing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly provisional CIT payments plus one annual final settlement filing
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly instalment payments are due within 15 days after the end of each calendar quarter; the annual return and true-up liability must be filed and paid by 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating revenue from NVOCC ocean freight forwarding, container brokerage, logistics agency, and ancillary services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare on an accrual basis the full invoiced consideration, including port, handling, document and booking commissions. A Chinese resident WFOE is taxed on worldwide income; do not treat cross-border freight earnings as automatically foreign-source. Reconcile revenue to VAT export invoices, house bills of lading, SWIFT wires, and ACH receipts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of operations: ocean carrier fees, port charges, container equipment, drayage, terminal handling, packing, insurance, and customs brokerage costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only documented costs supported by compliant Chinese VAT special invoices, non-resident tax vouchers, and written service agreements. Payments to offshore affiliated carriers without substantive service evidence are at risk of disallowance and recharacterization as dividend distributions subject to 10% withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxes and surcharges other than CIT: urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, stamp duty, real estate and land-use taxes, and other business taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only taxes actually borne by the WFOE in the PRC. VAT collected from Chinese clients is not deductible. A WFOE acting as a foreign principal agent must ensure VAT invoicing is performed by the correct Chinese taxable entity to avoid shadow execution and PE risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling and distribution expenses, including commission, marketing, ocean freight solicitation, and customer relationship costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Commissions paid to non-resident ocean freight agents are deductible only if the agent does not create a permanent establishment for the WFOE in China and the commission rate is arm's length. A zero-markup commission arrangement without CUP benchmarking will be challenged.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General and administrative expenses: payroll, rent, office, professional fees, head-office cost allocations, and management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A WFOE must not simply pay a percentage-of-revenue management fee to its foreign parent. A proper service agreement, cost contribution evidence, low-margin TNMM support, and audited records must exist; otherwise the payment is a transfer pricing red flag and may be disallowed entirely.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial expenses: interest on bank and intercompany loans, bank charges, foreign exchange losses, and guarantee fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party interest is subject to China thin-capitalisation control at a 2:1 debt-to-equity ratio for non-financial entities. Interest paid to a non-resident enterprise is also subject to 10% withholding before treaty relief. The WFOE must withhold, remit, and obtain tax vouchers before it can deduct the interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total accounting profit before tax under PRC Accounting Standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the audited financial statements to the return. Unreported container freight rebates, off-book kickbacks, or cash settlement of NVOCC charges create CIT evasion exposure for the legal representative and finance director.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments: add-backs of non-deductible expenses, entertainment expense caps, advertising limits, depreciation differences, and related-party interest disallowance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete Schedule A105000 and transfer pricing sub-schedules for all cross-border payments. If contemporaneous documentation is absent, the tax authority may use Article 44 of the CIT Law to infer taxable income, shifting the burden of proving arm's length pricing to the WFOE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after carryforward of qualified prior-year tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only losses from timely filed NVOCC operations and only at the same taxpayer entity level. Losses of a foreign parent or non-resident PE cannot be offset against WFOE profit through a group loss-sharing mechanism.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Base CIT at 25%, subtract foreign tax credits, quarterly paid instalments, and compute final tax payable or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Schedule A108000 if a foreign tax credit is claimed. For a captive NVOCC intermediary, artificially low Chinese profit inconsistent with actual freight volume, container count, and turnover will trigger a full re-examination and tax re-assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-exempt income, reduced-rate income, and special incentives such as 15% high-tech or regional preferential treatment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A free-zone or encouraged-industry entity must obtain the applicable qualification certificate and prove real operations. A shell NVOCC with no staff, no office, no booking capability, and no cargo control cannot claim preferential tax rates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 / Schedule D and related-party statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction summary, contemporaneous documentation declaration, and transfer pricing methodology schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the annual related-party transaction forms in the CIT package. Use CUP or TNMM for intercompany freight services. Local File is mandatory when related-party service transactions exceed CNY 100 million; Master File is due where group-wide related-party volume triggers the higher threshold.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing of an annual CIT return attracts a CNY 2,000 to CNY 10,000 administrative fine under Article 62 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law; unpaid tax accrues a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05%. Under Article 63, deliberate concealment or false return causing underpayment triggers penalties of 50% to five times the underpaid tax plus criminal referral. Failure to file transfer pricing forms or Local/Master File documentation creates additional penalties, and fraudulent filings attract criminal imprisonment thresholds.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends distributed by a Chinese WFOE to non-resident corporate shareholders; treaty-reduced rates are available where the beneficial owner is the tax resident of a treaty jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the foreign shareholder must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its jurisdiction of residence, submit a beneficial ownership declaration through the Chinese withholding agent to the State Taxation Administration, evidence shareholding exceeding the treaty's 25% threshold if a lower dividend rate is claimed, provide board resolutions and audited accounts proving no conduit arrangement, and file the reduced withholding before the dividend payment date. The Chinese tax authority can deny relief under the Principal Purpose Test and issue a written determination disallowing treaty benefits if the WFOE is a mailbox entity with no economic substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on outbound royalties and interest paid by a Chinese WFOE to a non-resident enterprise is 10%. Treaty rates commonly reduce interest to 7%-10% and royalties to 5%-10% depending on the jurisdiction. Interest is also subject to thin-capitalisation and transfer pricing review; royalties paid to an offshore mailbox company that does not own or control the intangible and does not perform Core Income-Generating Activities will be recharacterised as service fees or dividends and denied treaty relief.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: China's Local File threshold triggers at annual related-party tangible-property transactions exceeding CNY 200 million; intangible-property, financial-asset, or service transactions exceeding CNY 100 million; and other related-party transactions exceeding CNY 40 million. Master File is required for a multinational group whose global annual related-party transaction volume exceeds CNY 1 billion or when the tax authority requires it due to high risk.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China applies substance-over-form through CIT Law Articles 41, 45 and 47, anti-avoidance rules, and the Place of Effective Management doctrine. Although China does not impose an ESR regime as named in offshore territories, a foreign-owned NVOCC must maintain real employees, offices, bank accounts, operating licences, and decision-making functions in China. The Core Income-Generating Activities of ocean freight forwarding—booking, load planning, carrier contracting, house bill of lading issuance, cargo tracking, claims handling, and revenue collection—must be performed by the Chinese WFOE and not by an offshore shell affiliate.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE deliberately under-declares NVOCC freight revenue by diverting container booking proceeds through an offshore sister company that issues no invoices to Chinese cargo customers, while the Chinese entity pays local container-terminal expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 63 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law imposes restitution plus a penalty of 50% to five times the underpaid CIT; Criminal Law Article 201 imposes fines and imprisonment up to seven years for fraudulent concealment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative, finance director, and actual controller face personal civil recovery, asset seizure, travel bans, blacklisting by the tax court, and imprisonment as responsible persons under PRC Criminal Law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Cost Invoicing / False VAT Special Invoices
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE buys or fabricates special VAT invoices from fictitious logistics companies to inflate deductible cost of sales and obtain falsely matched input VAT credits, including circular container-detention fee invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal Law Article 205 punishes false special VAT invoice issuance or use with fines and imprisonment up to life imprisonment where the false amount is huge; Tax Collection and Administration Law Article 63 adds underpaid tax penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts pierce the corporate veil when the invoice transaction is a sham; the director is jointly and severally liable for tax debt, faces personal confiscation of assets, permanent exit blacklisting, loss of bank access, and criminal imprisonment as principal or accomplice.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / AML and Foreign Exchange Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE is a shell with no China-based freight operations; overseas collections are settled through private offshore accounts, cross-border payments are routed to conceal beneficial ownership, and USD freight receipts are not repatriated through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange system, creating an AML freight-laundering red flag.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law and SAFE regulations permit fines from 5% to 30% of the illegal transaction amount plus confiscation; Criminal Law Article 191 punishes money-laundering with fines and imprisonment up to ten years for serious cross-border proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who knowingly benefits from the shell structure loses corporate veil protection: personal assets are subject to restitution, the director is blacklisted from SAFE cross-border transactions and banking services, travel is restricted by court order, and criminal imprisonment up to ten years may be imposed.
